title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.intervention: Addition of rhenium (Re) to the alloy
recollection.structure: Likely a single-phase solid solution with Re incorporated, possibly affecting defect structures
recollection.mechanism: Re addition may alter defect formation energies, suppressing irradiation-induced damage such as dislocation loops or voids
recollection.results: Presumably, the alloy with Re shows improved resistance to irradiation, quantified by lower defect densities or reduced swelling compared to NbMoTaW without Re

score.note: The recollection identifies Re addition and the broad improvement in irradiation resistance, but this is largely evident from the title. It generically suggests a single-phase solid solution and defect suppression, without recalling grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, defect-sink behavior, or suppression of grain-boundary He bubbles. No irradiation conditions, mechanical-property values, bubble measurements, or other quantitative results are provided.
